data.narrative: Completed Module 1 containerization - chose Debian Slim base image for compatibility with native dependencies, understood multi-stage build benefits (smaller images, security), identified layer caching issues (COPY . . before npm install causes cache invalidation), applied security hardening (non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, .dockerignore). Fixed build issues by reordering Dockerfile instructions and adding comprehensive .dockerignore.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose Debian Slim over Alpine for notification service with native dependencies (bcrypt, database drivers). Understood trade-off: larger size (80MB vs 5MB) but better compatibility and debugging. Applied security hardening with non-root user (appuser), HEALTHCHECK instruction, and .dockerignore.
dimension_scores.evidence: Base image decision: 'Debian Slim uses glibc which most packages expect, fewer surprises, better debugging tools available'

dimension_scores.observation: Chose multi-stage build strategy to separate builder stage (with build tools, dev dependencies) from runtime stage (only needed files). Identified that multi-stage produces smaller images by excluding build tools and dev dependencies from final image.
dimension_scores.evidence: Build strategy decision: 'Multi-stage separates builder stage from runtime stage. Smaller final image means faster downloads, smaller attack surface, fewer security vulnerabilities'

dimension_scores.observation: Added HEALTHCHECK instruction with 30s interval, 5s timeout, 10s start-period, 3 retries. Health checks include /live (process up) and /ready (dependencies ready) endpoints for proper traffic routing during startup.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verification summary: 'Health checks - /live endpoint checks if process is running, /ready endpoint checks if dependencies are ready, matters for traffic routing during startup'

dimension_scores.observation: Identified two build issues: slow builds due to layer cache invalidation (COPY . . before npm install), and sensitive files in image due to missing .dockerignore. Understood root causes and fixes for both issues.
dimension_scores.evidence: Break step diagnosis: 'Dockerfile likely has COPY . . before RUN npm install, so any source file change invalidates install layer and forces full dependency reinstall'

dimension_scores.observation: Module 1 focused on containerization rather than degradation design. Set baseline score. Understanding of health checks (/live vs /ready) provides foundation for degradation patterns in later modules.
dimension_scores.evidence: No degradation-specific exercises in Module 1 - focused on containerization fundamentals

dimension_scores.observation: Created comprehensive reflection documentation covering comprehension questions, mini practical task with layer caching demonstration, risk/mitigation analysis, and key takeaways. Documentation is clear and actionable.
dimension_scores.evidence: module1_reflection.md includes layer caching commands with proof, risk analysis of secrets in images, and mitigation strategy

strengths: Chose Debian Slim over Alpine based on service requirements (native dependencies) rather than defaulting to smaller size
Identified layer caching issue root cause and fix (reorder COPY instructions)
Applied comprehensive security hardening (non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, .dockerignore)
Understood multi-stage build benefits for image size and security
data.recommendation: Continue to Module 2 to develop pipeline design skills - CI/CD pipeline structure, stage separation, failure handling, and deployment safety.

public_evidence.student_action: Chose Debian Slim base image for compatibility, applied multi-stage build strategy, added non-root user (appuser), implemented HEALTHCHECK instruction, created comprehensive .dockerignore to exclude secrets and unnecessary files
public_evidence.technical_detail: Debian Slim base image (glibc for compatibility), multi-stage Dockerfile with builder/runtime stages, RUN groupadd/useradd for appuser, HEALTHCHECK with 30s interval/5s timeout/10s start-period/3 retries, .dockerignore excluding .git, node_modules, .env.*, tests
public_evidence.ability: Building production-ready containers with security hardening and optimization
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates understanding of containerization best practices including base image selection, multi-stage builds, layer caching, security hardening, and build optimization - critical skills for deploying reliable services

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: module1_reflection.md demonstrates COPY package.json before COPY . . to preserve npm install cache
Base image decision explains multi-stage benefits: 'separates builder stage from runtime stage, smaller final image, smaller attack surface'
Fix step includes non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, and .dockerignore for secrets exclusion
